title: Phoenixville Hospital earns top marks in two care areas
summary: U.S. News & World Report's 2026-27 Best Hospitals ratings gave the 144-bed Tower Health facility "high performing" designations for rehabilitation and for heart attack treatment, the highest mark in its procedures-and-conditions scoring. Fewer than half of the roughly 4,500 hospitals reviewed nationally earned recognition in any category.

title: A Phoenixville family took in a skateboarder crossing the country for his brother
summary: Skyler King left Oxford, Mississippi on Aug. 1 on a 1,100-mile skateboard trip to New York City in memory of his brother Justin, raising money for suicide prevention along the way, and a Phoenixville family he met on the road opened their home to him as he passed through. He reached southeastern Pennsylvania this week with under 100 miles left.

title: Phoenixville's Sly Fox closes its Pittsburgh taphouse
summary: Sly Fox Brewing, founded in Phoenixville in 1995, chose not to renew the lease on its downtown Pittsburgh taphouse, which poured its last beers Aug. 15 after five years on Liberty Avenue. The Pennsylvania locations in Phoenixville, Pottstown, Malvern and Wyomissing stay open, and Pittsburgh gift cards remain good at them.

title: Ocean State Job Lot opens at the Shoppes at Valley Forge
summary: The discount chain opened its first Chester County store on Tuesday, Sept. 8, filling the former Big Lots at 260 Schuylkill Road. A grand-opening event follows Saturday, Sept. 12, when the first 100 customers between 9 a.m. and noon receive a gift card worth $10 to $100.

title: 6abc features Bluebird's new pizza room on Bridge Street
summary: Bluebird Distilling's Phoenixville home now doubles as a pizzeria, and 6abc's FYI Philly put the made-over space on TV. Owner Jared Adkins added an open kitchen turning out handmade pies with local toppings, plus a fireplace dining room, a bar over the street and a patio seating more than two dozen.

title: The Drift is serving seafood on Bridge Street
summary: The Drift Seafood Kitchen & Raw Bar is up and running at 231 Bridge Street, marking Labor Day weekend as its first holiday stretch open. Hours run 4 to 10 p.m. Monday through Thursday, 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday, and 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. Sunday.

title: Marching bands from 15 schools head to Phoenixville on Sept. 19
summary: The Phoenixville Marching Phantoms host their annual Phestival of Bands on Saturday, Sept. 19 at Phoenixville Area High School, drawing 14 visiting high school bands plus Millersville University's ensemble. Concessions, raffles and student-made origami cranes round out a night that doubles as the fundraiser for the school's marching arts program.

title: Colonial Theatre lays out a fall run of films, concerts and Halloween nights
summary: The Bridge Street theater's fall calendar runs Sept. 11 through Nov. 14, mixing tribute concerts, independent and cultural films and comedy with a month of horror programming in October. Anchors include the Exhumed Films 24-hour Horror-thon on Oct. 17 and a HUSH speakeasy night closing the season Nov. 14.

title: Phoenixville Film Festival returns with 62 films, including a steel-town premiere
summary: The fourth annual festival takes over the Colonial Theatre Sept. 17-20 with 62 films, four world premieres and 23 Pennsylvania premieres, plus master classes, panels and workshops. Two entries are close to home: Steel Wheel, a world premiere on the borough's steelmaking history, and The Haunting of Pennhurst. Tickets run $5 to $25.

title: Amtrak deal moves a Phoenixville train stop closer to reality
summary: Amtrak and the Schuylkill River Passenger Rail Authority signed an agreement to plan and develop passenger service linking Reading, Pottstown, Phoenixville and Philadelphia, a corridor with no trains since 1981. The authority hopes construction starts by 2028 and service around 2030.
